title: Redwood discovery: model selection - Summit AI
summary: Discovery focused on model selection for Summit AI's multi-lingual assistant. Discussed context length requirements (8k vs 32k vs 128k), open-model tradeoffs, tool-calling / function-calling support, hosted vs dedicated vs private deployment (data residency, KMS, SSO), and a proposed pilot to benchmark latency/cost with Summit's 50% Spanish traffic. Agreed next steps: send security pack, run benchmark on 8k & 32k contexts, schedule technical deep dive, and provide pricing options for Hosted vs Dedicated pilot.
next_steps: Redwood: Share security pack + SOC2 + KMS notes (Priya) - due 2025-12-15
Redwood: Run perf benchmark (8k vs 32k) on a subset of Summit prompts (Jordan) - target 2025-12-19
Customer: Provide 10 sample prompt sets and latency SLOs (Maya) - due 2025-12-16
Schedule technical deep-dive for infra team (Priya + Lina) - propose times 2025-12-18 or 2025-12-19
action_items: Priya Patel (SE) - Send security docs link and SOC2 evidence by 2025-12-15
Jordan Lee (Solutions) - Run dedicated vs hosted perf bench (8k/32k) and share spreadsheet by 2025-12-19
Maya Rodriguez (Head of ML) - Share 10 canonical prompts and 50 convo examples by 2025-12-16
Lina Park (Infra) - Confirm networking constraints for Private deployment (VPC peering, no public egress) by 2025-12-17
transcript:
00:00 Alex Chen: Hey everyone thanks for joining, this is Alex from Redwood, I'm joined by Priya our SE and Jordan on solutions. Hi all.
00:25 Maya Rodriguez: Hey Alex, thanks, we appreciate you making time. Quick intro: I'm Maya, Head of ML at Summit AI. Our app is a multi-lingual conversational assistant for customer support, about 50% Spanish traffic, some French and Japanese.
00:52 Ethan Kim: Ethan here, CTO, mainly listening for infra constraints and security.
01:10 Alex Chen: Great. High level - we want to understand model selection needs: context length, tool-calling, latency SLOs, and deployment mode (hosted/dedicated/private).
01:34 Priya Patel: Quick Q - what are your current models & infra? Are you on OpenAI today or self-hosted?
01:50 Maya Rodriguez: We have a hybrid. Prototyped on OpenAI for ease of dev; also running internal Llama 2 13B for some inference on prem. Costs are creeping up so we're evaluating options. 
02:12 Sahil Verma: For a lot of our domain tasks we need about 8k of context, but for some legal/records flows we want 32k; long-term we'd like to support very long contexts (100k) for transcript summarization but that's less urgent.
02:35 Priya Patel: Makes sense. So likely you'll want a model family with reasonable 32k support; not all open models handle 32k efficiently. Are hallucination/quality a big concern?
02:52 Maya Rodriguez: Quality is critical for support answers, hallucinations hit SLA. Also we need tool-calling to fetch customer account data and DB lookups, so function-calling is required.
03:12 Jordan Lee: Quick clarification on tool-calling - do you need Redwood to host tools or just support function-calling semantics and webhooks?
03:25 Lina Park: We prefer webhooks to our internal APIs; but egress is restricted - we may need a VPC/private option so calls don't traverse public internet.
03:40 Priya Patel: Understood. So Hosted API works for most teams, but for your egress constraints Dedicated or Private (VPC/on-prem) might be necessary. We can do private control plane with customer-managed networking and KMS integration.
04:05 Ethan Kim: On KMS - we use AWS KMS and want to hold keys. Can Redwood integrate with customer-managed KMS/HSM?
04:22 Priya Patel: Yes - Redwood Private supports customer KMS/HSM for encryption at rest and can mute logging for sensitive fields. For Dedicated we have options too (bring-your-own-key via AWS KMS).
04:45 Maya Rodriguez: SOC2 and audit logs are must-haves. Can you share evidence?
04:55 Alex Chen: Absolutely; we'll send SOC2, penetration test summaries, and our audit log schema.
05:10 Sahil Verma: Back to models - what open models do you recommend for 8k vs 32k?
05:22 Priya Patel: For 8k workloads, many of the Llama-family forks and MPT variants are reasonable; for 32k we'd look at models like Mistral-Long, Falcon-40B-instruct variants or open long-context optimized checkpoints. Redwood's model catalog includes performance profiles and we can recommend quantization levels.
05:48 Maya Rodriguez: Any differences in function-calling support across models? We rely on consistent function-calling, JSON output and tool invocation.
06:02 Jordan Lee: Function-calling is largely orchestration-layer behavior; we provide structured output tools/parsers - for some open models you need additional output-format prompts or light post-processing. Our SDK provides function-calling primitives that work across hosted and private setups.
06:28 Maya Rodriguez: We also need multi-lingual quality; some models degrade in Spanish. Do you have curated evals?
06:38 Priya Patel: Yes, Redwood Optimize has eval suites - we can run your Spanish/French/Japanese prompt-sets through candidates and return BLEU/ROUGE-ish metrics plus human pass/fail samples. That's what we'd propose during the pilot.
06:58 Ethan Kim: Latency SLOs - we target 100-300ms token latency for short-turn interactions, and <2s for typical responses. Can Redwood hit that?
07:14 Priya Patel: Depends on model size and infra. Hosted with smaller optimized models can hit sub-200ms, Dedicated GPU pools with batching and KV cache can improve throughput but may add micro latency for batch waits. We can tune batching policies for your 95th percentile.
07:40 Maya Rodriguez: Cost is big - we may accept slightly higher latency if unit cost is 40-50% cheaper than OpenAI. Can you provide cost comparisons?
07:55 Alex Chen: We will. Pricing options vary: Hosted pay-as-you-go, Dedicated reserved capacity, Private with licensing. We'll include comparative unit economics in the pricing doc.
08:12 Sahil Verma: Regarding KV cache, we've heard Redwood has prefix/KV caching - is that automatic?
08:24 Priya Patel: We have automatic prefix/KV caching for repeated contexts (like system prompts, recent turns); it reduces per-token compute. It's configurable. Sometimes the transcription shows 'KV cash' in our notes, it's actually KV cache.
08:40 Lina Park: On networking - if Private, will we need to deploy an on-prem package or can you run inside our VPC?
08:52 Jordan Lee: Both options: Private VPC integration or on-prem package for air-gapped. We'll need to review the network diagram and egress rules.
09:10 Maya Rodriguez: For benchmark pilot: we want Redwood to run a 1-week pilot comparing a hosted setup (smaller LLM) vs dedicated 32k-optimized model. Key metrics: latency P50/P95, token cost, quality (human eval on 200 samples), and failure modes for tool calls.
09:38 Priya Patel: That aligns with what we typically do. We'll ask you to share canonical prompts and a small set of production traces.
09:52 Ethan Kim: Security question again - do you support SSO (SAML/Okta) and per-user RBAC?
10:05 Alex Chen: Yes SSO with SAML/OAuth, SCIM for provisioning, RBAC for roles. Audit logs are available for Dedicated and Private with extended retention add-on.
10:20 Maya Rodriguez: Any lock-in concerns? We want ability to move between Hosted and Dedicated without major rewrites.
10:33 Priya Patel: That's a core Redwood goal - same API surface across Hosted/Dedicated/Private so you can pin model versions and rollout policies with minimal code changes.
10:50 Sahil Verma: On quantization - how aggressive can we go while keeping Spanish quality? We've seen some methods degrade non-English fluency.
11:05 Priya Patel: We recommend per-model quantization profiles. We'll test 4-bit/8-bit mixes during the pilot and validate against your Spanish eval set. We err on the side of less aggressive quant when quality matters.
11:28 Maya Rodriguez: Great. Any constraints on tool-calls per-request? We sometimes have 2-3 external API calls per turn.
11:40 Jordan Lee: We support multi-step tool-calling and structured json function returns. For Private with limited egress we can route tool calls through a customer-hosted proxy.
12:00 Maya Rodriguez: About on-device/offline - we might want a later phase for a fully on-prem inference for EU data residency; is that feasible?
12:15 Priya Patel: Yes, our Private on-prem package supports air-gapped installs; that's typically an enterprise engagement with professional services.
12:30 Ethan Kim: OK. Can you also confirm model update practices and rollbacks? We'll need canary deploys and automatic fallback to a stable variant.
12:44 Alex Chen: Yes, Redwood Console supports canary rollouts, A/B tests, automatic fallback policies based on error rate or quality regressions.
13:00 Maya Rodriguez: Good. For the pilot, what instruments will you provide for observability? We need token-level cost, per-route latency, error traces.
13:15 Priya Patel: Redwood Console provides token-level cost, latency breakdowns, per-route dashboards, and tracing hooks to attach to your telemetry. We'll include sample screenshots in the pack.
13:30 Sahil Verma: A few quick clarifying Qs - 1) Do you support incremental KV cache warmup across restarts? 2) Can we pin model weights to a specific variant?
13:46 Jordan Lee: 1) Yes cache warmup persists in Dedicated; 2) Yes you can pin versions and rollback.
14:00 Maya Rodriguez: Any legal constraints around training on customer data? We don't want models retrained on our PII.
14:12 Alex Chen: Redwood does not train customer data; hosted models are inference-only. We can sign contractual clauses restricting data usage and ensure no training on customer inputs.
14:30 Ethan Kim: Excellent. Cost question - what's the expected RPS throughput on a single Dedicated GPU pool for a 13B vs 40B model?
14:48 Priya Patel: Rough ballparks: optimized 13B variants can do hundreds of rps with batching on high-end GPUs; 40B will be lower throughput but higher quality. We'll provide a throughput/latency table for your target GPU types in the follow-up.
15:10 Maya Rodriguez: On competitor comparison - we like the simplicity of OpenAI but want cost savings and more control; also evaluating Anthropic for safety and Replicate for multi-cloud ease.
15:30 Alex Chen: Makes sense. Redwood focuses on production economics and predictable serving - unified runtime across environments with fallbacks.
15:45 Maya Rodriguez: Any gotchas with function-calling across models? We rely on structured outputs to then call internal microservices.
15:58 Jordan Lee: Some open models need better prompt engineering; our SDK adds a wrapper around model outputs and offers stricter JSON schema validation and auto-retries on parse failures.
16:15 Lina Park: About networking again - if we run Private in our VPC, how do we handle secret provisioning and key rotation?
16:30 Priya Patel: We integrate with your KMS for secrets and recommend short-lived instance roles; key rotation is managed by your KMS policies. We'll share our key lifecycle guide.
16:50 Maya Rodriguez: Great. For the pilot, we want Redwood to measure Spanish quality and hallucination rate. Will you do human evaluations?
17:03 Priya Patel: Yes, we'll run human evals on a sample set and provide side-by-side comparisons across model candidates.
17:25 Alex Chen: Recap: Redwood sends security pack + SOC2 docs; customer shares prompts; Redwood runs 1-week pilot comparing Hosted smaller LLM vs Dedicated 32k optimized variant; deliverables: latency/cost/quality spreadsheet and recommended model.
17:48 Maya Rodriguez: That sounds right. Timeline workable for us.
18:02 Ethan Kim: One last Q - if we start with Hosted pilot and later move to Dedicated, what's typical migration time?
18:18 Priya Patel: Usually 2-6 weeks depending on capacity and networking if Dedicated GPUs reserved; Private on-prem tends to be longer with professional services.
18:35 Maya Rodriguez: Thanks - let's set the tech deep-dive for next week.
18:42 Alex Chen: I'll follow up with proposed times. Thanks everyone.
18:50 [Call end]
notes: Security pack link: https://redwood.ai/security/summit-pack (will be sent)
